The climate of French cities, 1951-2025

What 25,027,470 daily records say about warming, extremes and rainfall in 20 large cities.

Generated on 22 November 2026 · 2,433 stations · 40 source files · reference normal 1991-2020

  • Warming is clear, and it is speeding up. +0.33 °C per decade since 1951 (95% CI: 0.28 to 0.39), +0.43 °C since 1981. All of the 10 warmest years came after 2010; the warmest was 2022 (+1.5 °C).
  • Summer is warming the fastest (+0.43 °C per decade). All 20 cities show a significant trend; Lyon is warming the most, Brest the least.
  • Hot extremes are multiplying. Days ≥ 35 °C × 5.5, tropical nights × 3.1, frost days −34%.
  • Annual rainfall shows no clear trend (−0.4% per decade, not significant). The decline in summer rainfall (−2.3% per decade) is borderline significant.
  • The data is reliable but must be handled with care. Very few values are rejected; the real issue is the continuity of the series (stations that close or move), handled by choosing stations carefully and splicing series.

Data and method

1. Collection40 CSV files discovered through the data.gouv.fr API and downloaded in parallel (268 MB).
2. WarehouseLoaded into DuckDB: 25.0 million typed rows in a few seconds.
3. QualityMétéo-France quality codes, physical bounds, TN ≤ TX consistency, duplicates.
4. StationsOne reference station per city, splicing of interrupted series.
5. AnalysisAnomalies, trends (OLS, Mann-Kendall, Theil-Sen), extremes, records, PCA + k-means.
  • Mean temperature = (TN + TX) / 2: the climatological convention, consistent over the whole period.
  • Validity: a month counts if at least 90% of its days have data, a year if at least 95% do.
  • National average: the mean of each city's anomaly against its own normal, so that different climates are not mixed.
  • Trends: linear regression (slope and confidence interval) confirmed by a non-parametric Mann-Kendall test; a trend is only called significant when both tests are, at the 5% level.

1. How much has France warmed?

Maximum and minimum temperatures are rising at the same pace (+0.34 and +0.32 °C per decade). Coldest year in the series: 1956 (−2.4 °C).

Annual total−0.4%p = 0.593not significant
Total · winter−1.5%p = 0.307not significant

Longest dry spell+0.14 dp = 0.295not significant

A "not significant" result is still a result: with year-to-year variability of around ±20%, 75 years of data are not enough to detect a change in annual totals. The driest year was 2022 (−24%).

Cross-validation against ERA5

Mean correlation of daily maximum temperatures: 0.987. Mean bias: −0.46 °C on maximum temperatures, +0.48 °C on minimum temperatures, peaking in Ajaccio (+4.7 °C on minimum temperatures).

Limitations

  • Non-homogenised series: only identified relocations are corrected; urbanisation around stations can amplify the measured warming.
  • A station represents a city, not its whole area.
  • The tests assume independent years: the p-values are slightly optimistic.
  • A linear trend is a poor summary of warming that has been speeding up since the 1980s.

Reproduce the analysis

pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m meteo all              # collection, warehouse, ERA5 validation, analyses, report
streamlit run dashboard/app.py   # interactive dashboard
